figures.caption: Figure 1. Visualizing the Curvature Hypothesis. The blue curve depicts a Stubborn Hallucination (sharp minimum), and the red curve depicts Generalized Knowledge (flat minimum). Although both converge to a low loss state, applying a small perturbation (blue dotted line) forces the hallucinated model up the steep walls of its basin, resulting in a large gradient vector. This geometric instability serves as the detection signal for our proposed EPGS metric.

Table 1. Comparison of General Hallucination Detection methods across Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Mistral-7B-v0.1 using BERTScore for labeling. We compare Black Box methods—Length-normalized Entropy (LNE), P (False) (PF), Semantic Entropy (SE), and Discrete SE (DSE)—and White Box methods—Eigenscore (ES) and Effective Rank (ER)—against our proposed method, EPGS. All values reported are AUROC scores (higher is better). The best results are highlighted in bold and the second-best results are underlined.

Table 8. Computational efficiency comparison on the TriviaQA dataset. Average Latency (seconds) and Peak VRAM (GB) are measured for processing 100 samples across Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Mistral-7B.
Figure 2. Qualitative examples showing the Question, Correct Answer, Pseudo-answer, and the calculated Curvature Score.

Table 4. Ablation study on the magnitude of Gaussian noise (ϵ) added during gradient sensitivity analysis. We compare performance across different noise levels ϵ ∈ {0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1} for Llama-2-7b and Llama-3-8b. The best result for each column is highlighted in bold.

Table 2. Performance comparison on the Stubborn Hallucination Subset across Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B using BERTScore for labelling. We evaluate Black Box methods (LNE, PF, SE, DSE) and White Box methods (ER, ES) against our proposed method (EPGS). All values are AUROC scores. The best results are highlighted in bold and the second-best results are underlined.
Table 7. Ablation study on the importance of Named Entity Recognition (NER). The best results are highlighted in bold.

Table 6. Ablation study comparing different perturbation strategies across Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B. We compare Prompt Perturbation methods (Empty, Neutral, Active, Reasoning, Noise), Paraphrasing, and Dropout against our proposed Embedding Perturbation (EPGS). All values are AUROC scores. The best performance in each column is highlighted in bold.

Table 5. Comparison of General Hallucination Detection methods across Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Mistral-7B-v0.1 using SQuAD-F1 for labeling. We compare Black Box methods (LNE, PF, SE, DSE) and White Box methods (ER, ES) against our proposed method (EPGS). All values are AUROC scores (higher is better).
